title: Platform ops procurement kit - SLA clauses & escalation playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact go-to-market + procurement-facing kit aimed at platform and infrastructure buyers (platform engineering, infra, SRE) evaluating Dedicated capacity. Focus: how to translate our technical isolation and throughput guarantees into contract language, measurable SLOs, and an operator-friendly escalation path.

Audience:
- Platform engineering leads and SRE managers who own procurement decisions
- Procurement and vendor-risk teams needing clear acceptance criteria and remediation clauses
- Solutions engineers and AE pre-sales who need quick, defensible answers during negotiations

Topline messaging (single-sentence):
Redwood Dedicated delivers guaranteed capacity with strict tenancy isolation, measurable throughput SLAs, and an operator-first escalation path so platform teams get predictable performance and clear contractual remedies.

Key claims and how to prove them (short):
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pools per tenant with cryptographic separation of control-plane metadata; proof: architecture diagram + teardown checklist + audit log sample (see linked Confluence).
- Predictable throughput: per-SKU tokens/sec and p99 per-request latency budgets derived from benchmark suite run against committed hardware. Proof: throughput report (CSV), sample load test, deploy runbook.
- SLA-backed uptime: defined uptime % per month + service credit schedule. Proof: prior customers on Dedicated (anonymized) + synthetic uptime trace.
- Operational observability: token-level cost & latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, and traces exposed via Console + exported to customer telemetry. Proof: sample dashboard screenshots and API export sample.

Measurements & definitions to include in contracts (explicit language suggestions):
- "Committed Throughput" definition: sustained tokens/sec for model X measured over 10-minute sliding windows, sustained for at least N concurrent streams.
- "Latency Budget" definition: p95/p99 generation latency for sequences of length L at the committed concurrency level.
- "Uptime" definition: percentage of calendar minutes in a monthly billing period where the tenant's dedicated pool is available for traffic (control plane incidents that do not affect data path excluded).
- "Isolation Failure" definition: any incident resulting in cross-tenant memory or KV-cache bleed, or unauthorized access to the tenant's checkout; requires post-mortem & remediation within 72 hours.

Sample SLA clause (editable):
- Uptime Guarantee: Redwood guarantees 99.95% monthly availability of the dedicated inference service for the committed SKU. If availability in a given month is below the guaranteed level, Customer will receive Service Credits as follows: 99.0–99.95% -> 10% credit of monthly Dedicated fee; 95.0–99.0% -> 30% credit; <95.0% -> 60% credit.
- Throughput Commitment: Redwood guarantees the Committed Throughput for the contracted model family under the agreed concurrency profile. Failure to meet Committed Throughput for three consecutive measurement windows entitles Customer to a remediation plan and, if not resolved within 7 business days, a 15% pro-rated credit for the affected period.
- Isolation & Data Controls: Redwood will not colocate customer workloads with third-party tenants on the same inference worker unless explicitly agreed and will ship audit logs showing worker assignment for each allocation request.

Escalation playbook (operator-facing):
- Tier 0: Customer observes degraded p99 for committed model. AE/Solutions opens a Support ticket (SL 15m for P1) and copies assigned SRE on-duty.
- Tier 1: On-call SRE verifies metrics; if issue is capacity-related, trigger immediate scale/burst from reserved burst pool (policy contained in runbook).
- Tier 2: If isolation-related concerns (memory bleed, KV cache overlap), SREs stop new allocations, snapshot affected workers for forensic analysis, and initiate cross-team war room.
- Post-incident: Joint RCA within 5 business days, remediation plan with timeline, and contractual credit calculation if SLA thresholds breached.

Proof points & artifacts to attach to procurement packet:
- Dedicated runbook excerpt (allocation lifecycle, eviction policy)
- Recent third-party latency & throughput report (anonymized)
- Architecture diagram highlighting segmentation boundaries and KMS integrations
- Example contract appendix with the SLA language above + operational contact template
- Onboarding checklist showing ramp phases (week 0–4) and acceptance tests

Procurement checklist for buyers (quick):
- Confirm SKU and bump schedule (how burst capacity is handled)
- Require monthly throughput reports + access to raw telemetry for first 90 days
- Add audit log delivery cadence and log retention window in contract (default 180 days for Dedicated)
- Define runbook handover: who is on-call, escalation contacts, and times for scheduled maintenance windows

Example AE talking track (2 min):
"Our Dedicated offering gives you a reserved pool tuned to your workloads — this is not just faster hardware, it's a contractable guarantee. We commit to a measurable throughput profile and p99 latency at your target concurrency. If we miss that bar, you'll have explicit remediation steps and service credits in the contract. For platform teams that need predictable user experience and billing, that certainty is the main ROI — fewer firefights, measurable cost per inference, and a clear playbook when things go sideways."

Competitive differentiators to highlight vs. infra vendors and cloud-managed endpoints:
- Unified product: identical API surface across Hosted and Dedicated lets you prototype on Hosted then commit capacity without code changes.
- Quality-preserving optimizations: automatic KV/prefix caching and batching tuned per-customer — keeps per-token cost down without sacrificing latency SLOs.
- Procurement-first artifacts: prebuilt SLA appendix, technical onboarding checklist, and audit log export that accelerate legal and procurement signoff.

Common buyer objections and suggested responses:
- "How do we know you'll hit the numbers?" -> share benchmark artifacts, invite a proof-of-concept run using customer prompts and traffic pattern simulation.
- "What if we need isolation beyond GPU-level?" -> provide private deployment options with customer-managed control plane + HSM/KMS integrations (see Private Deployment brief).
- "What about burst costs?" -> transparent burst pricing and pre-authorized burst limits; include an explicit budget cap in the contract.

Open questions / work items (internal):
- Define exact measurement thresholds for "Committed Throughput" across our top 6 SKUs — PR for metrics team (JIRA-4821).
- Legal: confirm service credit ladder and whether credits are the exclusive remedy for outages.
- Solutions: create a 30-minute POC template that can be run against customer traffic with guidance for redaction/PKI.

Notes to legal and product ops (callouts):
- Keep remediation timeline practical — we need 7 business days for complex isolation investigations. Flag if customer requests shorter windows.
- Add a clause for force-majeure that excludes cloud provider outages but not Redwood software regressions.

Attachment ideas for packet to customer:
- 1-page sell sheet (visual), 2-page SRE runbook excerpt, sample SLA appendix (editable Word), onboarding timeline (spreadsheet), and a 45-min workshop agenda for platform ops.

Quick next steps (owner: Priya):
- Convert this draft into a 1p sell sheet + editable SLA appendix (due EOD next Tuesday).
- Sync with Metrics (Ethan) to finalize measurement definitions (target: next Wed).
- Schedule a dry-run workshop with Legal to validate credit ladder language (Carlos to coordinate).

Unresolved negotiation knobs (for AE playbook):
- Burst pool guarantee: optional vs. included in base SKU
- Audit log retention length vs. cost

-----
Notes-to-self (rough): keep examples concrete — customers want numbers not fuzzy promises. Follow up with anonymized customer throughput graphs. Link in progress: Confluence page for reserved capacity playbook (see linked_artifacts).
